report.source_text: Six days after the initial presentation, the patient presented to the ED again with increasing back and left lower extremity pain, confusion, auditory hallucinations, and fever for three days. He was tachycardic to 109 bpm and febrile to 101-102F (38.8C). Neuromuscular examination demonstrated 2/5 strength in bilateral lower extremities. He was unable to perform hip flexion and leg elevation. Sensation was grossly intact throughout both lower extremities. He had a white blood cell count of 24,000/mcL with a lactate of 2.8 mmol/L. The patient was also found to be in diabetic ketoacidosis with a blood glucose of 588 mg/dL, an anion gap of 26, and a pH of 7.35.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 40-year-old male with a history of diabetes mellitus and ethanol use initially presented to the ED several days after being struck by a motor vehicle, complaining of worsening back pain and difficulties on ambulation. Initial CT spine showed a nondisplaced L2 vertebral body fracture. Six days later, the patient re-presented to the ED with increasing back and left lower extremity pain, confusion, auditory hallucinations, and fever (101-102F). He was tachycardic (109 bpm), had a white blood cell count of 24,000/mcL, lactate of 2.8 mmol/L, and was in diabetic ketoacidosis with a blood glucose of 588 mg/dL. Subsequent imaging revealed an L2 paraspinal soft tissue mass with multilocular low attenuation changes in the left psoas muscle, raising concern for an infected hematoma or intramuscular abscess. Interventional radiology performed percutaneous drainage of 20 mL of purulent material from the left psoas muscle, which was positive for Methicillin-sensitive Staph Aureus (MSSA). An MRI later confirmed bilateral psoas abscesses. Subsequent fluid collections in the left gluteal region, right psoas, and posterior thigh were also drained, though cultures from these later drainages were negative. The patient received intravenous cefazolin therapy, leading to symptom alleviation and eventual discharge after a ten-week hospital stay.
